deck.name: World Geography
deck.description: Capitals, oceans, rivers, mountains and world records, then regional geography, climate, map skills and political geography.

questions.prompt: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers more area than all of Earth's land combined.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.explanation: It stands about 8,849 m (29,032 ft) high.

questions.prompt: Which river is usually listed as the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: Some studies argue the Amazon is longer; the answer depends on how the source is measured.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers less than half a square kilometer, about a fifth of a square mile.

questions.prompt: What is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Russia covers about 17 million km², more than a ninth of Earth's land.

questions.prompt: Which country has had the largest population since 2023?
questions.explanation: UN estimates show India passing China in 2023.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was built as the capital as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa, not Toronto, is the capital. Queen Victoria chose it in 1857.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as the capital in 1960.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Ankara replaced Istanbul as the capital in 1923, when the Republic of Turkey was founded.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Abuja replaced Lagos as the capital in 1991.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington has been the capital since 1865. Auckland is the largest city.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.explanation: Asia covers about 30% of Earth's land area and has more people than any other continent.

questions.prompt: Africa has more countries than any other continent.
questions.explanation: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations.

questions.prompt: What is the deepest known point in the ocean?
choices: Horizon Deep in the Tonga Trench
Sirena Deep in the Mariana Trench
Milwaukee Deep in the Puerto Rico Trench
Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench
questions.explanation: It is about 10,900 m (roughly 35,800 ft) deep.

questions.prompt: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal, in Russia, is about 1,640 m deep.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake by surface area?
questions.explanation: Despite its name, the Caspian Sea is usually classed as a lake, because land surrounds it.

questions.prompt: What is the longest continental mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Andes run the full length of western South America, through seven countries.

questions.prompt: What is the largest island in the world (not counting continents)?
questions.explanation: Australia is larger, but it counts as a continent.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates Spain from Morocco?
questions.explanation: The strait links the Mediterranean Sea with the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect?
questions.explanation: The canal opened in 1914 and uses locks to lift ships about 26 m above sea level to cross Panama.

questions.prompt: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
questions.explanation: At 5,895 m, Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain.

questions.prompt: Which country contains most of the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explanation: About 60% of the Amazon rainforest lies in Brazil.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest point on land?
choices: The shore of the Dead Sea
questions.explanation: It lies more than 400 m below sea level.

questions.prompt: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: Counting cold deserts, Antarctica is the largest desert overall.

questions.prompt: Bolivia and Paraguay are the only landlocked countries in South America.
questions.explanation: Bolivia lost its coastline to Chile in the War of the Pacific (1879 to 1884).

questions.prompt: Through which place does the Prime Meridian (0° longitude) pass?
questions.explanation: The meridian through the Royal Observatory in Greenwich was adopted internationally in 1884.

questions.prompt: How many continents are there in the most common model taught in English-speaking countries?
questions.explanation: Other models join the Americas, or Europe and Asia, giving five or six continents.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan moved its capital from Almaty to Astana in 1997. The city was named Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022.

questions.prompt: Which country is crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.explanation: Brazil is the only country crossed by both lines.

questions.prompt: Which country is divided into the regions of Flanders, Wallonia, and Brussels-Capital?
questions.explanation: Belgium is a federal state with three regions: the Dutch-speaking Flanders, French-speaking Wallonia, and bilingual Brussels-Capital.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range forms much of the boundary between France and Spain?
questions.explanation: The Pyrenees extend between the Bay of Biscay and the Mediterranean, separating the Iberian Peninsula from France.

questions.prompt: The Po River drains much of which part of Italy?
questions.explanation: The Po flows east across northern Italy into the Adriatic Sea.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between the Balkan Peninsula and Anatolia?
questions.explanation: The Aegean Sea is part of the eastern Mediterranean between Greece and Türkiye.

questions.prompt: Which European capital stands on the River Vltava?
questions.explanation: The Vltava flows through Prague before joining the Elbe.

questions.prompt: Which country has coastlines on both the Adriatic and Ionian seas?
questions.explanation: Albania has a western coast on the Adriatic and a southern coast on the Ionian Sea.

questions.prompt: The Transfăgărășan road crosses which mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Transfăgărășan crosses the Făgăraș Mountains, part of Romania’s Southern Carpathians.

questions.prompt: Which country occupies most of the Jutland Peninsula?
questions.explanation: Most of Jutland belongs to Denmark, while its southern portion is in Germany.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Lyon and joins the Rhône?
questions.explanation: The Saône meets the Rhône in Lyon in southeastern France.

questions.prompt: Which island group belongs to Portugal and lies in the North Atlantic?
questions.explanation: The Azores are an autonomous region of Portugal located in the mid-Atlantic.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the autonomous region of Gagauzia?
questions.explanation: Gagauzia is an autonomous territorial unit in southern Moldova.

questions.prompt: Which strait links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara?
questions.explanation: The Bosphorus passes through Istanbul and connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara.

questions.prompt: Which country is home to the Svalbard archipelago?
questions.explanation: Svalbard is a Norwegian archipelago in the Arctic Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which river forms a large part of the border between Germany and Poland?
questions.explanation: The Oder, together with the Lusatian Neisse, forms much of the Germany–Poland border.

questions.prompt: Which capital is located at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers?
questions.explanation: Belgrade lies where the Sava joins the Danube in Serbia.

questions.prompt: Which body of water separates mainland Greece from the Peloponnese at the Corinth Canal?
questions.explanation: The Corinth Canal cuts through the narrow Isthmus of Corinth, connecting the Gulf of Corinth with the Saronic Gulf.

questions.prompt: Which country surrounds the Italian enclaves of Campione d’Italia and, almost entirely, Vatican City?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is an enclave within Rome, while Campione d’Italia is an Italian exclave surrounded by Switzerland.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Porto before reaching the Atlantic?
questions.explanation: The Douro crosses northern Portugal and enters the Atlantic at Porto.

questions.prompt: Which country is crossed by the Tropic of Cancer and contains the Thar Desert?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses northern India, and the Thar Desert lies mainly in India and Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the ancient city of Varanasi?
questions.explanation: Varanasi stands on the Ganges in northern India.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip reaching toward China?
questions.explanation: The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow eastern extension of Afghanistan between Tajikistan and Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Which inland sea lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan?
questions.explanation: The Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan and has dramatically shrunk because of river diversion.

questions.prompt: Which country is separated from the Korean Peninsula by the Korea Strait?
questions.explanation: The Korea Strait lies between South Korea and the Japanese islands.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Cambodia’s capital, Phnom Penh, and meets the Mekong there?
questions.explanation: The Tonlé Sap River links the Great Lake with the Mekong and meets it in Phnom Penh.

questions.prompt: Which two countries share the island of Borneo with Brunei?
questions.explanation: Borneo is divided among Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates much of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau?
questions.explanation: The Himalayan chain forms a high natural barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Fergana Valley along with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan?
questions.explanation: The Fergana Valley spans parts of Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.

questions.prompt: Which strait separates the Malay Peninsula from the Indonesian island of Sumatra?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca is a major shipping route between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the ancient city of Samarkand?
questions.explanation: Samarkand is a historic city in Uzbekistan and an important Silk Road center.

questions.prompt: Which river system drains much of mainland Southeast Asia and flows through Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam?
questions.explanation: The Mekong flows through or along six countries and forms a large delta in southern Vietnam.

questions.prompt: Which country’s capital, Ulaanbaatar, is one of the world’s coldest national capitals?
questions.explanation: Ulaanbaatar has a strongly continental climate and very cold winters.

questions.prompt: Which desert occupies much of the Arabian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Desert spans most of the Arabian Peninsula, including the Rub’ al Khali.

questions.prompt: Which major river flows through Baghdad?
questions.explanation: Baghdad is situated on the Tigris; the Tigris and Euphrates form much of Mesopotamia’s river system.

questions.prompt: Which Asian country is made up of more than 7,000 islands and has Manila as its capital?
questions.explanation: The Philippines is an archipelago in the western Pacific with Manila as its capital.

questions.prompt: Which gulf lies between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Persian Gulf is a semi-enclosed sea between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Sundarbans, a vast mangrove region shared with India?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans span southwestern Bangladesh and adjacent eastern India in the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta.

questions.prompt: Which African lake is a major source region of the White Nile?
questions.explanation: The White Nile’s headwater system includes streams flowing from the Lake Victoria basin.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Atlas Mountains and borders both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Morocco has Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts and includes the western Atlas ranges.

questions.prompt: Which river forms much of the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe?
questions.explanation: The Zambezi forms part of the Zambia–Zimbabwe border and flows over Victoria Falls.

questions.prompt: Which African country has the exclave of Cabinda separated from its main territory by a strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
questions.explanation: Cabinda is an Angolan exclave on the Atlantic coast, separated from the rest of Angola by the DRC.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the ancient rock-hewn churches of Lalibela?
questions.explanation: Lalibela in Ethiopia is famous for its medieval rock-hewn churches.

questions.prompt: Which African river flows north through Sudan and Egypt?
questions.explanation: The Nile flows north through Sudan and Egypt to the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.prompt: Which country’s capital is Windhoek?
questions.explanation: Windhoek is the capital of Namibia, in southwestern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which highland region is shared by Ethiopia and Eritrea?
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian Highlands extend into Eritrea and form the headwaters of several regional rivers.

questions.prompt: Which island country lies east of Mozambique and is known for its distinctive lemur fauna?
questions.explanation: Madagascar is a large island off southeastern Africa; most lemur species are native there.

questions.prompt: Which African country is crossed by the Equator and includes the Rwenzori Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Equator crosses Uganda, where the Rwenzori range rises along the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

questions.prompt: Which river forms a large inland delta in Botswana?
questions.explanation: The Okavango River spreads into a large seasonal delta in the Kalahari Basin rather than reaching the sea.

questions.prompt: Which country occupies most of the Cape Verde archipelago?
questions.explanation: Cabo Verde is an island country in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of West Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the port city of Mombasa?
questions.explanation: Mombasa is a major port on Kenya’s Indian Ocean coast.

questions.prompt: Which South American country has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean?
questions.explanation: Colombia borders both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean.

questions.prompt: Which branch of the Amazon River flows through Manaus before joining the Rio Negro?
questions.explanation: The Solimões reaches Manaus; its confluence with the Rio Negro forms the lower Amazon, called the Amazonas downstream.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Atacama Desert’s northern portion?
questions.explanation: The Atacama is an extremely arid region along northern Chile’s Pacific coast.

questions.prompt: Which country contains the Guiana Highlands and the Angel Falls?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls drops from Auyán-tepui in Venezuela’s Guiana Highlands.

questions.prompt: Which South American capital is situated at high altitude in the Andes and serves as Bolivia’s seat of government?
questions.explanation: La Paz is Bolivia’s administrative capital and one of the world’s highest major cities; Sucre is the constitutional capital.

questions.prompt: Which river is formed by the confluence of the Paraná and Uruguay rivers before reaching the Atlantic?
questions.explanation: The Paraná and Uruguay rivers meet to form the broad Río de la Plata estuary between Argentina and Uruguay.

questions.prompt: Which country shares the Llanos tropical grasslands with Venezuela?
questions.explanation: The Llanos extend across Colombia and Venezuela in the Orinoco basin.

questions.prompt: Which country is crossed by the equator and has the Galápagos Islands as a province?
questions.explanation: The Galápagos are part of Ecuador, whose mainland is crossed by the Equator.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Rosario in Argentina?
questions.explanation: Rosario is an important port on the Paraná River.

questions.prompt: Which archipelago is shared by Ecuador and lies about 1,000 kilometers west of its mainland?
questions.explanation: The Galápagos lie in the Pacific Ocean west of Ecuador and are internationally known for endemic wildlife.

questions.prompt: Which South American country has Georgetown as its capital?
questions.explanation: Georgetown is the capital of Guyana, on the northern Atlantic coast.

questions.prompt: Which climate classification describes a region with very little precipitation and sparse vegetation?
questions.explanation: Arid climates receive little precipitation relative to potential evaporation.

questions.prompt: On a topographic map, what do closely spaced contour lines usually indicate?
questions.explanation: Closely spaced contour lines show that elevation changes rapidly over a short horizontal distance.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the line where a river’s drainage basin is separated from a neighboring basin?
questions.explanation: A drainage divide is high ground that separates the flow of water into different basins.

questions.prompt: Which map projection is designed to preserve area proportions?
questions.explanation: Equal-area projections preserve relative area, though shape or scale may be distorted.

questions.prompt: What is a river delta?
choices: A deep glacial valley that has been flooded by the sea
A ring of coral reef enclosing a shallow central lagoon
A sediment-built landform at a river mouth where it enters standing water
A ridge of high ground separating two neighboring watersheds
questions.explanation: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it enters a sea or lake.

questions.prompt: Which ocean current contributes to relatively mild winters in western Europe?
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Drift, an extension of the Gulf Stream system, transports warm water toward western Europe.

questions.prompt: What is an exclave?
choices: A part of a country separated from its main territory by foreign territory
A country with no coastline, surrounded entirely by other countries
A region governed jointly by two countries that share sovereignty
A small territory that one country leases from another for a fixed term
questions.explanation: An exclave is separated from the main part of its state by the territory of another state.

questions.prompt: Which line of latitude lies at approximately 66.5 degrees north?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Circle marks the approximate southern limit of at least one day of midnight sun each year in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas?
questions.explanation: An isthmus joins larger land areas while separating bodies of water.

questions.prompt: Which term describes a seasonal reversal of prevailing winds that often brings a rainy season?
questions.explanation: Monsoon systems involve seasonal shifts in winds and often produce marked wet and dry seasons.

questions.prompt: What does a map scale of 1:100,000 mean?
choices: One unit on the map represents 100,000 of the same units on the ground
One kilometer on the map equals one meter on the ground
The map is one hundred thousand times larger than the landscape
questions.explanation: A ratio scale compares identical units, so one centimeter represents 100,000 centimeters, or one kilometer.

questions.prompt: Which type of boundary follows a mountain crest or watershed rather than a straight survey line?
questions.explanation: Physical boundaries use natural features such as ridges and rivers as dividing lines.

questions.prompt: Which ocean basin contains the Mariana Trench?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific Ocean.

questions.prompt: What is a fjord?
choices: A fan of sediment deposited where a river meets the sea
A salt lake left behind in an arid, enclosed basin
A chain of volcanic islands formed above a hotspot
A deep, narrow sea inlet formed in a glacially carved valley
questions.explanation: Glacial erosion carves steep-sided valleys that can later flood with seawater to form fjords.

questions.prompt: Which region is defined by the watershed of a river and its tributaries?
questions.explanation: A river basin is the land area drained by a river system.

questions.prompt: A country can have territory on more than one continent.
questions.explanation: Russia and Türkiye, among others, have territory conventionally assigned to more than one continent.

questions.prompt: Every point on the Equator experiences exactly 12 hours of daylight every day of the year.
questions.explanation: Day length near the Equator changes little through the year but is not exactly 12 hours every day because of atmospheric refraction and the Sun’s apparent disk.

questions.prompt: A watershed boundary generally follows higher ground between neighboring drainage areas.
questions.explanation: Ridges and other high ground separate runoff flowing into different river systems.

questions.prompt: The International Date Line follows the 180-degree meridian exactly along its entire route.
questions.explanation: The line generally follows the 180-degree meridian but bends around national territories and island groups.

questions.prompt: The Andes extend along the western edge of South America.
questions.explanation: The Andes form a long mountain chain near South America’s Pacific coast.

questions.prompt: An archipelago is a group or chain of islands.
questions.explanation: The term describes an island group, whether the islands are clustered or spread across a region.

questions.prompt: All rivers flow from north to south.
questions.explanation: Rivers flow downhill under gravity, so their directions depend on terrain rather than compass direction.

questions.prompt: A conformal map projection preserves local angles but can distort area.
questions.explanation: Conformal projections preserve local shape and angles while area distortion increases away from their standard lines.

questions.prompt: A delta forms where a river erodes a deep valley into a mountain range.
questions.explanation: A delta is primarily depositional and forms near a river mouth where flow slows.

questions.prompt: The Caspian Sea is an endorheic basin with no natural outlet to the ocean.
questions.explanation: The Caspian is the world’s largest inland body of water and has no natural connection to the global ocean.

questions.prompt: What is a drainage divide?
questions.answer: High ground that separates runoff flowing into neighboring river basins.
questions.explanation: Rain falling on opposite sides of a divide flows toward different drainage systems.

questions.prompt: What is a strait?
questions.answer: A narrow waterway connecting two larger bodies of water.
questions.explanation: A strait can also separate two land areas, as the Strait of Malacca separates Sumatra from the Malay Peninsula.

questions.prompt: What is an alluvial fan?
questions.answer: A fan-shaped deposit of sediment where a stream leaves steep terrain and spreads onto flatter ground.
questions.explanation: As a stream loses speed at the base of a mountain, it drops sediment in a widening fan.

questions.prompt: What is a rain shadow?
questions.answer: A relatively dry area on the leeward side of a mountain range after moist air loses precipitation on the windward side.
questions.explanation: Descending air on the leeward side is often warmer and drier, producing a rain-shadow effect.

questions.prompt: What does a choropleth map use to show geographic data?
questions.answer: Shading or color intensity across areas to represent a value or category.
questions.explanation: A choropleth map commonly shades countries, states, or districts according to a statistical measure.

questions.prompt: What is a continental shelf?
questions.answer: The gently sloping, submerged edge of a continent extending from the coast to the continental slope.
questions.explanation: The shelf is shallow compared with the deep ocean basin and is part of the continent’s submerged margin.

questions.prompt: What is an atoll?
questions.answer: A ring-shaped coral reef or island surrounding a lagoon, commonly built around a subsiding volcanic island.
questions.explanation: Atolls develop as coral continues growing near sea level while the volcanic island beneath it subsides.

questions.prompt: What does “landlocked” mean for a country?
questions.answer: It has no coastline along an open sea or ocean.
questions.explanation: A landlocked state may still border lakes or rivers but lacks direct ocean access.

questions.prompt: What is an estuary?
questions.answer: A coastal area where river freshwater mixes with seawater.
questions.explanation: Estuaries are influenced by tides and provide habitat where fresh and salt water mix.

questions.prompt: What is a geodetic datum?
questions.answer: A reference model and coordinate framework used to locate positions on Earth.
questions.explanation: A datum specifies an Earth model and origin so geographic coordinates can be interpreted consistently.
